ambiguities_or_notes: Tolstoy’s entire unsent complaint, including the barber metaphor and every specific textual grievance, is translated without softening its severity.

The audited Markdown preserves printed note numeral 2 as a bare “2” after the rhetorical question about the story of his childhood but supplies no corresponding footnote definition; the seven surviving Markdown footnotes map to printed notes 1 and 3–8. The bare 2 is retained and omitted Soviet note 2 is not imported.
The provincial dog-word двошат is transliterated as dvoshat/dvoshali rather than guessed at; the editors’ own note identifies it as a provincialism and records that Tolstoy later used “breathed.”
The distinction between the icon of his angel and the portrait of his mother is preserved, as is the editorial explanation that censorship required the substitution.
All three embedded editorial notes and seven surviving Markdown footnotes are translated in full.
